# Independent measure audit of intrinsic reflection parity correlation

Audited independently by the depth/Helly route:

    candidate 93cf42ea22bcd767
    supporting computation verify_intrinsic_reflection_parity_correlation.py

Result: PASS after the author's explicit Borel-test qualification in the
convex-order paragraph. The exact test-function identity, attainment,
intrinsic Jacobian, parity reweighting, and moment/covariance formulas
all hold. The now-resolved wording point is recorded in Section 4 below.
No stronger retention or depth conclusion is inferred.

## 1. The measure, q=0, and null fibers

Compactness of C gives only finitely many nonempty integer fibers. A
nonempty convex fiber has Hausdorff dimension equal to its affine
dimension, so q is their maximum and is an integer. Every q-dimensional
compact convex fiber has positive finite H_q measure; every smaller
fiber has zero H_q measure when q>0. The disjoint lifted fibers are
isometric to their continuous-coordinate copies, and their measures add.
Thus M=sum_(z in P)w_z is positive and finite.

For q=0 each nonempty convex fiber is a singleton. There are finitely
many such points; H_0 is exactly counting measure and P contains all
nonempty fibers. None of the derivations purifies a fractional atom or
substitutes an integral for an atomic count.

If an intersection K_z intersect (2x-K_w) has positive H_q measure,
both source fibers have dimension q. Contributions involving a smaller
fiber are null. The ordered-pair formula therefore loses no positive
mass. Conversely a positive term forces the center's fiber to have
dimension q by the midpoint argument below, so R=0 on fibers outside P.

## 2. Alignment and the exact 2^(-q) factor

For z,w in P of the same parity, j=(z+w)/2 is integer and convexity puts
(K_z+K_w)/2 inside K_j. The direction of the Minkowski sum is L_z+L_w.
Its dimension is at least q, while the containing integer fiber has
dimension at most q. Hence both q-dimensional directions agree, K_j
also has dimension q, and its affine hull is their affine midpoint.
This checks both direction and translation; there is no unjustified
common direction assumption across different parity classes.

After writing K_z=a+A and K_w=b+B in the common Euclidean q-space L,
the midpoint variable is x=(a+b)/2+xi. The correlation integrand is

    integral_A 1_B(2xi-eta) dH_q(eta).

Its support lies in (A+B)/2 and therefore in the actual midpoint fiber.
For a test function defined only on S, it may be extended by zero off
S when this integral is written on the whole affine space. For fixed eta,
the substitution zeta=2xi-eta has determinant 2^q in orthonormal L
coordinates. Thus dH_q(xi)=2^(-q)dH_q(zeta), exactly as printed.
There is no determinant involving n+d, no angle between the contributing
fiber measures, and no multiplicity factor beyond the explicitly ordered
source pairs.

Tonelli applies to a nonnegative Borel test function. Bounded signed
functions follow by decomposition because the measures are finite.
For q=0 the same computation is a finite ordered-pair sum and its factor
is one. Its midpoint belongs to the unique singleton at the integer
midpoint base by convexity.

## 3. Upper semicontinuity and compact attainment

S is compact, being C intersect the closed mixed lattice. For a center
y in S, reflection sends the mixed lattice to itself. Consequently

    R(y)=integral_S 1_C(2y-a) dmu(a)

is exactly the retained H_q measure. If y_k tends to y within S, closedness
of C gives the pointwise upper-semicontinuity inequality for its indicator.
Applying Fatou to 1-1_C(2y_k-a), equivalently reverse Fatou to the bounded
indicators, gives limsup R(y_k)<=R(y). This proof retains all positive
boundary mass and applies unchanged to q=0. It also establishes the
needed Borel measurability.

Thus R attains its maximum on S. The positive exact average implies that
a maximizing center lies in P. Cauchy--Schwarz over the represented parity
classes gives precisely the printed weak bound. The retained measure
is centrally symmetric about its actual mixed center; every containing
CLOSED halfspace has at least half its mass even if the cutting boundary
has positive measure. This justifies the weaker depth certificate and
nothing stronger.

## 4. First and second moments and the parity bias

For each class, the independent ordered-pair first moment of (a+b)/2 is
M_r m_r. Its unnormalized second moment is

    (M_r Q_r+m_r m_r^T)/2.

Multiplying by the intrinsic factor 2^(-q) verifies equations (7) and
(12), including their powers of two. Normalizing the master identity
selects parity r with probability M_r^2/A, A=sum_r M_r^2, then averages
two independent points from mu_r/M_r. Its mean is sum_r M_r m_r/A.
This is generally different from the original mean sum_r m_r/M.

The comparison source nu=A^(-1)sum_r M_r mu_r is a probability measure
with exactly the same mean as the midpoint law eta. Pairwise Jensen gives
the stated convex-order comparison with THIS law, not with mu/M. The
test class is now explicitly stated as convex BOREL functions (or, as in the usual
convex-order definition, continuous convex functions on the full ambient
space). A finite convex function specified only on a closed convex set
can have nonmeasurable values at extreme boundary points; an unqualified
integral of every such function is therefore not defined. For finite
Borel convex tests, adding an affine lower bound gives the usual extended
integrals; for integrable convex tests all values are finite. This is a
test-class wording correction, not a defect in the Jensen argument or
any of the moment identities. The exact covariance difference is

    E_nu[yy^T]-E_eta[yy^T]
      =(1/(2A))sum_r(M_r Q_r-m_r m_r^T)
      =(1/(2A))sum_r M_r V_r,

and subtracting the common mean outer product leaves the same formula.
Each summand is positive semidefinite. This checks the full ambient base
and continuous cross-moments, not just the continuous variance.

## 5. Concrete checks and scope

The supplied verifier returns PASS for the interval mass/first-moment
integrals, the exact q=0 counting example, and the perpendicular-fiber
example. I separately checked the latter geometry: the two perpendicular
segments at bases 0 and 1 generate an ambient three-dimensional tetrahedron
whose only integer fibers have q=1. Their class moments give correlation
mass (2^2+4^2)/2=10 and full first moment (8,2,24), exactly as stated.

These calculations confirm why pairwise same-parity affine alignment is
sufficient and why global fiber alignment would be false. The result is
a one-step reflection-correlation identity with explicit parity bias;
it does not establish iteration preserving densities, a stronger universal
reflection-retention constant, or a new mixed centerpoint bound.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
